finding: Measured fp32 inference memory is parameter-dominated for the tested GPT-style models.
evidence: Average non-parameter memory fraction is about 7.42%.
why_it_matters: Sparse parameter compression can significantly affect estimated total memory when sparsity is high enough.

finding: Low sparsity can increase total memory under unstructured sparse storage.
evidence: At 25% sparsity, average estimated total-memory reduction is -46.29%.
why_it_matters: Index metadata can outweigh savings when too many weights remain nonzero.

finding: 50% sparsity is approximately the total-memory break-even point in this model.
evidence: At 50% sparsity, average estimated total-memory reduction is 0.00%.
why_it_matters: This matches the parameter-memory break-even behavior from Day 48/49.

finding: High sparsity gives meaningful total-memory savings.
evidence: At 75% sparsity, average total-memory reduction is 46.29%; at 90%, it is 74.06%.
why_it_matters: Sparsity only becomes useful when sparsity is high enough and sparse storage is supported.

finding: This is still an analytical approximation, not real sparse runtime profiling.
evidence: Sparse total memory is estimated using unchanged non-parameter memory and analytical sparse parameter memory.
why_it_matters: Real sparse runtime depends on sparse kernels, hardware support, sparse format, and workload shape.
